blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Growing trade tensions between the United States and China are reshaping traditional trade relationships, creating an opportunity for Southeast Asia to forge new economic partnerships, said Ayala Corp. chair Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala. Zobel de Ayala sees the rivalry between the two economic superpowers as a major “swing factor” for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean), whose members seek to maintain business ties with Washington and Beijing. “As a grouping of nations, I think we’ve managed to continue doing business with both, and I consider that a win at a time when the world is becoming polarized,” […]...
